findings:
1) GAO-HAN-LI-ZHOU (JFE 2018, 129:394-414, "Market intraday momentum"): Using SPY 1993-2013, the FIRST half-hour return (measured from prior close) predicts the LAST half-hour return; statistically/economically significant, robust to quoted and effective spreads, stronger on volatile/high-volume/recession/macro-news days; also present in 10 other active ETFs including QQQ; mechanisms proposed are infrequent portfolio rebalancing (Bogousslavsky 2016) and late-informed trading (ScienceDirect S0304405X18301351; Monash open-access PDF). CRITICAL SCALE CAVEAT: this is a once-per-day, 30-minute-aggregation effect that trades only the final 30 minutes — it is NOT evidence for minute-scale trend-following.

2) POST-PUBLICATION PERFORMANCE: Rosa (Journal of Futures Markets 2022, 42(12):2218-2234, "Understanding intraday momentum strategies") extends Gao et al. with ~7 years of post-sample data and finds "the predictability disappears in the out-of-sample period"; only signal-strength/regime-conditional (Markov-switching, threshold) versions retain any value. This matches the general publication-decay literature: McLean & Pontiff (JF 2016) — across 97 predictors, returns are 26% lower out-of-sample and 58% lower post-publication; Falck/Rej/Thesmar (arXiv 2105.01380) — Sharpe ratios of 72 published strategies roughly halve after publication. Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens (JFE 2021, "Hedging demand and market intraday momentum") is the strongest surviving evidence: across 60+ futures (equities, bonds, commodities, FX) 1974-2020, rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes, attributed to market-maker/leveraged-ETF GAMMA HEDGING demand, and the effect REVERTS over subsequent days — i.e., it is a mechanism-specific end-of-day flow effect, not generic intraday trend persistence.

3) MINUTE-SCALE TREND PERSISTENCE — EVIDENCE IS AGAINST: Safari & Schmidhuber (arXiv 2501.16772, "Trends and Reversion in Financial Markets on Time Scales from Minutes to Decades", using 14 years of futures tick data among other sources) find markets are in a TRENDING regime only from "a few hours to a few years" and in a REVERSION regime at shorter (minute/sub-hour) and much longer scales. Microstructure literature consistently documents significant NEGATIVE autocorrelation of index-futures returns at 1-5 minute horizons (bid-ask bounce, tick-boundary oscillation), with the negative-autocorrelation horizon shrinking over time (up to ~20 min in 1984-96, ~10 min by 1991-2001, shorter since). Most directly on point: Mesfin (arXiv 2605.04004, May 2026, independent researcher, NOT peer-reviewed but methodologically transparent with pre-locked decision log) tested 14 OHLCV signal families (ORB, gap fill/continuation, volume-spike momentum, session breakouts, liquidity-grab fades, news drift) on MNQ 5-minute RTH bars Dec 2021-Aug 2025 (947 days, NinjaTrader data) with a 2.0-point round-trip friction assumption: NOTHING passed (criteria: OOS walk-forward T>=2.0, N>=30, positive net, year-consistency). Key quantitative result: a "gross edge ceiling" of ~0.07-1.50 points per trade from bar-level OHLCV features vs a 2.0-point friction floor; volume-spike "momentum" had T~0 on N>2,000 (a precise null); MNQ Hurst 0.59 (momentum-dominant at 5-min) yet the between-bar tradeable residue is below cost; momentum "exists inside a bar" but is consumed before bar-close execution. The only survivors in that study hold 60-75 minutes, not 5-30 minutes (and are the author's own self-reported "positive controls" — treat with skepticism).

4) SMALL-TRADER 1-MINUTE NQ/ES AFTER-COST EXPECTANCY — ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE: I found NO peer-reviewed source documenting sustained positive after-cost expectancy for 1-minute-scale trend following in NQ/ES by small traders. The closest positive claims are non-peer-reviewed practitioner work: Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon (SSRN 4824172, 2024, SPY intraday trend-following with dynamic trailing stops, 2007-2024, claimed 19.6%/yr net, Sharpe 1.33) — single instrument, leverage-dependent, and an independent QuantConnect replication at 1x leverage found Sharpe ~0.40 with fees consuming ~16.7% of returns across 6,940 orders; reviewers (Hunt Gather Trade, quantmacro) flag single-instrument overfitting risk and non-traditional publication venue. Population-level evidence is strongly negative: Chague/De-Losso/Giovannetti (SSRN 3423101, "Day Trading for a Living?") tracked 19,646 individuals who began day-trading Brazilian index futures (world's #3 by volume) 2013-2015: 97% of those persisting >300 sessions lost money, only 1.1% earned above minimum wage, and there was NO evidence of learning over time.

implications: (1) REFRAME THE EDGE HYPOTHESIS: The literature's only robust intraday effect is END-OF-DAY momentum (rest-of-day return predicting the last 30 minutes, gamma-hedging channel, Baltussen 2021) — and our red-team already found that 279 session-close-exit trades carry the ENTIRE +$189.6k edge while trailing-stop exits net -$42.8k. That is exactly what a decayed Gao/Baltussen-style hold-into-close effect plus long drift would look like when wrapped in a 1-minute trend state machine. TEST: build the preregistered benchmark "enter on morning/rest-of-day direction, hold to 17:00 close, no intraday trailing logic" and a long-only drift benchmark; if Solar Wave RK does not beat both after costs, the vendor indicator adds nothing and the 1-minute machinery is costume. (2) EXPECT THE WFO/DSR GATES TO FAIL and do not soften them: minute-scale is a documented reversion regime (Safari-Schmidhuber; negative 1-5 min autocorrelation literature), and the closest same-instrument study (Mesfin, MNQ) found a 0.07-1.50 pt gross-edge ceiling vs a ~2-pt friction floor for bar-close-executed OHLCV signals — our own slip sensitivity (net -19% at 1 tick, -37% at 2 ticks; avg trade $40.83 ≈ 8 NQ ticks) sits uncomfortably close to that floor once real spread-crossing and stop slippage in fast markets are priced. Treat 2-tick results as the base case, not the stress case. (3) PRICE IN PUBLICATION/CROWDING DECAY: Gao et al.'s own effect disappeared out-of-sample (Rosa 2022), and the 26-58% haircut of McLean-Pontiff is the right prior for any effect our backtest shares with published anomalies; apply at least a 50% Sharpe haircut to the 1.39 in-sample figure when sizing the locked-forward evaluation, which puts the lower bound near zero given SE ~0.97. (4) The Baltussen mechanism is REGIME-DEPENDENT (gamma positioning) and REVERTS next-day — consistent with our Thursday/2024Q3 concentration; add a preregistered conditioning analysis on realized-vol / gamma-proxy regimes rather than rescue-tuning after failure. (5) Population evidence (97% of persistent index-futures day traders lose; no learning) plus the absence of ANY credible published case of sustained after-cost 1-minute trend-following profitability in NQ/ES means the burden of proof is entirely on our locked-forward period; no capital deployment before the freeze-tagged out-of-sample window completes.
verdict_component: Published research offers essentially no support for forward profitability of 1-minute trend-following in NQ as such: the peer-reviewed intraday-momentum literature validates only a once-daily, half-hour-scale end-of-day effect (Gao et al. 2018; Baltussen et al. 2021), the flagship version of which demonstrably disappeared out-of-sample after publication (Rosa 2022, JFM), while minute-scale horizons in liquid index futures are documented as a mean-reversion/microstructure-noise regime and the only same-instrument systematic study (MNQ, 2021-2025) found gross edges of 0.07-1.50 points per trade — below any realistic friction floor — with zero of fourteen signal families surviving; no credible source documents sustained after-cost 1-minute trend-following profitability for small traders in NQ/ES, and census-level evidence shows 97% of persistent retail index-futures day traders lose money. The literature is, however, strikingly consistent with our red-team decomposition: the strategy's entire edge living in hold-into-session-close trades is the signature of a (decayed, regime-dependent, gamma-hedging-driven) end-of-day momentum effect plus bull-market drift, not of genuine minute-scale trend detection — so the prior for the preregistered WFO/DSR gates should be failure, the 2-tick slippage case should be treated as the base case, and any surviving edge should be attributed to and tested against an explicit hold-into-close benchmark before a single contract trades live.

findings: SPREAD AND DEPTH. NQ is liquid by contract count (~600k contracts/day vs ES ~2M per damnpropfirms/edgeful comparisons) but has a structurally THIN book: practitioner microstructure sources (Bookmap NQ instrument page, edgeful ES-vs-NQ) consistently describe "only a handful of contracts at each price level" vs "hundreds" stacked on ES; tradealgo's NQ guide puts typical quoted spread at 0.25-0.50 points (1-2 ticks) with "hundreds of contracts within a few ticks" (i.e., cumulative across levels, not at BBO). A measured practitioner dataset (Astreka, "trade-time spread" by hour) reports NQ average spread of 2.32 ticks at its tightest hour (3pm hour), ~2.3-2.7 ticks across liquid cash hours, and 5.51 ticks at the 18:00 ET reopen — implying overnight/off-hours spreads run 2-5x RTH. CME's own institutional TCA ("Big Picture" cost comparison) prices an NQ round trip at ~10.4 bps total including an assumed 5 bps market impact for block size — consistent with sub-tick half-spread cost only for RTH top-of-book executions. MEASURED 1-LOT SLIPPAGE: PickMyTrade's aggregation of ~1,000 live retail futures fills reports average market-order slippage of 0.8-1.2 ticks/trade during peak hours on NQ (Rithmic-connected ~0.7, Tradovate ~1.2, IB 0.8-1.0, NinjaTrader feeds 0.9-1.5), worst case 3-5 ticks around news, and 5-20 ticks during CPI/FOMC/NFP releases; Optimus/PickMyTrade education notes ES spreads can blow out to 2-4 points at FOMC with the book emptying ("liquidity vacuum"); Global Trading reported S&P 500 futures book depth declined ~90% at the height of the April 2025 tariff turmoil — a bear/stress regime your 2023-2025 sample never contains. THE 16:59:30-17:00 ET MINUTE. Session structure (CME contract specs / hours guides): equity index futures halt 16:15-16:30 ET, trade a post-settlement session 16:30-17:00 ET, then the daily maintenance break 17:00-18:00 ET. NQ's daily settlement VWAP window is 15:14:30-15:15:00 CT = 16:14:30-16:15:00 ET (CME Client Systems Wiki; other equity indices use 14:59:30-15:00:00 CT per the CME education course) — so your exit minute is NOT the settlement window; it sits 45+ minutes after settlement in the thinnest half-hour of the listed day, where sources uniformly describe tapering volume and wider spreads. However, that final minute is NOT dead: Apex Trader Funding requires all funded accounts flat by 4:59 PM ET with auto-liquidation, and NinjaTrader's default ExitOnSessionCloseSeconds=30 means an entire ecosystem of retail/prop strategies fires market orders at exactly 16:59:30 — your exit is time-synchronized with a crowd of correlated flatting flow hitting a thin post-settlement book. CRITICAL PLATFORM MECHANIC (NinjaTrader support forum, official answers): ExitOnSessionCloseSeconds is REAL-TIME ONLY; in Strategy Analyzer backtests, IsExitOnSessionCloseStrategy fills the exit at the CLOSE PRICE OF THE LAST BAR of the session (the 17:00:00 print), with no spread. Live, the same strategy sends a market order at 16:59:30 into a 1-2+ tick-wide book. Your 279 session-close trades — which carry the entire +$189.6k net edge — are therefore backtested with a fill mechanism that does not exist live: last-print fill at T vs bid/ask-crossing fill at T-30s. BREAK-EVEN ARITHMETIC from your own numbers: each additional tick/execution costs 2,915 trades x 2 executions x $5 = ~$29,150 over the sample (matches your slip-0 -> slip-1 -> slip-2 deltas of ~$27.8k/$26.7k); slip-0 net $146.4k implies mechanical break-even at ~5 ticks/execution, but PF is already 1.081 at 2 ticks — statistical significance dies far before mechanical break-even.
implications: 1) Re-rate the base case: 1 tick/execution is a defensible CENTRAL estimate only for RTH normal-condition executions (measured retail averages 0.7-1.2 ticks), but it is NOT conservative for this strategy because entries occur across the full ETH session (spreads 2-5x wider off-hours) and profit concentrates in the thin 16:30-17:00 post-settlement window. Treat the 2-tick line (net $91.9k, PF 1.081) as the realistic planning case, and keep the 1-tick line as optimistic. 2) Fix the session-close fill mechanic before trusting the 279 edge-carrying trades: NinjaTrader backtests fill EOSC at the last bar's close price while live fires a market order at 16:59:30. Preregister a variant that exits with an explicit timed market order at 16:58 or 16:59 (so backtest and live use the same mechanism and price bar), and measure edge decay when the exit moves 1/2/5 minutes earlier — if the +$189.6k concentration collapses when exiting at 16:55, the edge is an artifact of last-print marking, not capturable price. 3) Add a state-dependent slippage overlay to the registry instead of a flat tick: ~1 tick RTH, ~2 ticks for 16:30-17:00 exits and any ETH executions, and 5-10 ticks for executions within +/-2 minutes of CPI/FOMC/NFP timestamps (your 5.5 trades/day market-order cadence guarantees event-window hits); rerun DSR/PBO on that overlay. 4) Quantify crowding risk at 16:59:30: your exit is synchronized to the second with NinjaTrader's default EOSC and one minute after Apex's 4:59 PM ET forced flattening — assume adverse selection when the day's trend-followers all exit the same side; the direct cost on 279 trades is small (~2-4 extra ticks = ~$3-6k total, not edge-killing), but log live fill-vs-backtest deltas as a first-class parity metric. 5) Before capital, run a live-sim/micro shadow on MNQ (1/10 notional, deeper contract-count book) for a few weeks specifically to measure realized slippage distribution at 16:59:30 and on entries; feed the empirical distribution back into the locked-forward evaluation. 6) Note for the regime-risk file: April 2025-style stress showed ~90% depth decline in index futures — slippage in the unseen bear regime will be materially worse than anything in the 2023-2025 sample.

verdict_component: The 1-tick-per-execution assumption is defensible as a central estimate for regular-hours 1-lot NQ market orders (measured retail fills average 0.7-1.2 ticks in peak hours), but it is not conservative for this particular strategy, and the slippage number is not even the main execution risk. The strategy's entire net edge sits in 279 exits executed in the thinnest tradable half-hour of the day (post-settlement 16:30-17:00 ET), and NinjaTrader's backtester fills those exits at the last bar's close print while live trading would send a market order 30 seconds earlier into a 1-2+ tick book, time-synchronized with Apex's 4:59 PM forced flattening and every other NinjaTrader default-EOSC strategy — a fill-mechanism mismatch the penny-exact Strategy Analyzer parity cannot detect because both sides of that parity share the same unrealistic fill model. Mechanically the strategy survives to ~5 ticks/execution and even pessimistic close-window slippage (2-4 extra ticks on 279 trades, roughly $3-6k) does not erase the $189.6k concentration, so slippage alone does not kill forward profitability; but the realistic planning case should be the ~2-tick line (PF 1.081), where statistical significance under DSR/bootstrap is already doubtful, and the sample contains no stress regime of the kind (April 2025) where index-futures depth fell ~90%. Forward profitability therefore hinges less on the tick assumption than on whether the session-close prices are achievable at 16:59:30 — which is testable pre-capital by re-running with explicit timed exits at 16:55-16:59 and by shadow-measuring live fills on MNQ, and both tests should gate the freeze tag.

findings:
CLASSIC LITERATURE (the null we tested against): Lou, Polk & Skouras (JFE 2019, "A Tug of War") document that US equity strategy profits split cleanly into overnight vs intraday components, with index drift accruing overwhelmingly overnight (http://personal.lse.ac.uk/polk/research/TugOfWar.pdf). Practitioner replications: ~93-98% of QQQ's gains since 1999 accrued close-to-open (Cacciatore, Medium 2025); NY Fed (1998-2019) finds the overnight session earned 2.6%/yr of the 4.3%/yr total S&P futures return, concentrated 2:00-3:00 AM ET at the European open, with a NEGATIVE "opening reversal" at 9:30 (libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org). Robot Wealth confirms the overnight dominance persisted in SPY through May 2024.

OUR EXACT WINDOW (computed from Yahoo Finance unadjusted daily OHLC, Dec-30-2022 close to Feb-28-2025 close, 541 sessions): QQQ close-to-close +90.8%; overnight (close→open) +50.1% cumulative; intraday RTH (open→close) +27.1% — i.e., 63%/37% overnight/intraday in log terms. Crucially the split was NOT classic: 2023 was an anomalous intraday-dominant year (intraday +38.9% vs overnight +10.7%), while 2024 reverted to classic (overnight +31.4%, intraday -5.0%) and Jan-Feb 2025 was overnight +3.2%, intraday -3.7%.

DOLLARIZED FOR 1 NQ CONTRACT (point-sums × $20, QQQ scaled ×41.1; cross-checks against NDX 10,939.76→20,884.41 = +9,945 pts = $198.9k): 24h buy-and-hold ≈ +$198.8k; overnight-only ≈ +$149.6k (75% of point gains); ALWAYS-LONG RTH-INTRADAY-ONLY ≈ +$49.2k (25%). (Continuous-contract NQ would be ~10% lower from financing-minus-dividend carry drag at 2023-25 rates; does not change conclusions.) Quarterly intraday-drift dollars: 2023Q1 +$47.8k, 2023Q2 +$31.2k, 2023Q3 -$19.0k, 2023Q4 +$26.5k, 2024Q1 +$8.9k, 2024Q2 +$0.4k, 2024Q3 -$27.7k, 2024Q4 -$2.8k, 2025Q1(Jan-Feb) -$15.9k. Intraday up-days 301 (avg +2.73 QQQ pts) vs down-days 240 (avg -3.18): intraday drift came from frequency of up days, not size.

LAST-HALF-HOUR LITERATURE: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (JFE 2018, SPY 1993-2013) — first half-hour return predicts last half-hour, R²≈1.6%, stronger on volatile/high-volume days. Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (JFE 2021) — across 60+ futures 1974-2020, rest-of-day return positively predicts the last 30 minutes ("market intraday momentum"), attributed to gamma-hedging flows from option market-makers and leveraged ETFs; the effect is TWO-SIDED (continuation on down days too) and REVERTS over subsequent days.

THE ARITHMETIC ON OUR STRATEGY: (1) If truly flat outside RTH, the maximum unconditional drift harvest is $49.2k — one-third of our $146.4k slip-0 net — and that requires 100% long exposure every RTH minute; a two-sided state machine with trailing stops has time-weighted NET long exposure far below 100% (plausibly 10-40%), bounding static-drift capture at roughly $5-20k, i.e., ≤15% of net. (2) The quarterly cross-check contradicts pure drift: our profit concentration (2024Q3+2024Aug+2025Jan ≈ 45% of net) falls in quarters where intraday drift was NEGATIVE (-$27.7k, -$15.9k); money made against the drift direction cannot be repackaged long-drift. (3) But conditional drift-TIMING is a live channel: long trend-start entries held to session close in a +91% tape capture far more than TWAP drift — this fits the long/short PF gap (1.20 vs 1.07) and the session-close bucket (+$189.6k, PF 10.8, ~$680/trade ≈ 19 bps of notional), and 2023's freak intraday-dominant drift means "flat overnight" did NOT immunize the 2023 portion of our P&L. (4) PREMISE FLAW FOUND: "flat every day at 17:00 ET" is the CME Globex session close; the Globex session spans 18:00→17:00, so unless the session template is RTH-only the strategy CAN hold through the 16:00→9:30 equity-overnight window — which carried 75% (~$150k/contract) of the drift, concentrated 2-3 AM ET. "Exit on session close" only guarantees flatness 17:00-18:00. The "flat overnight" claim is unverified from timestamps.
implications: CONCRETE ACTIONS FOR THIS CAMPAIGN: (1) Audit the trade ledger NOW: compute contract-hours of long and short exposure by clock hour; report the share in (a) 9:30-16:00 RTH, (b) 16:00-9:30 overnight Globex window, (c) the 2-3 AM ET drift hour, (d) the last 30 min before session close. If overnight-window long exposure is material, the drift-confounding ceiling rises from ~$49k toward ~$150k and the whole "intraday-only" defense collapses. (2) Add a beta-carry decomposition to the preregistered analysis: regress daily MTM P&L on same-day NQ close-to-close return, and separately on the overnight and RTH components; report beta, beta×mean-return (drift carry in $), alpha, and alpha t-stat, per year and pooled. Gate the freeze tag on alpha surviving with the drift carry removed. (3) Register and run long-only and short-only variants: in a +91% tape, short-side PF 1.07 with positive net is evidence AGAINST pure drift — quantify it; also split P&L by calendar year (if 2023 P&L share ≫ 2024-25 share, drift-timing suspicion rises since 2023 held the +$86k intraday drift). (4) Run a detrended synthetic test: subtract the window's mean per-1-min-bar drift from prices and re-run; the surviving P&L approximates the non-drift edge. (5) Reframe the session-close bucket: part of it is the documented two-sided last-30-min momentum (gamma-flow-driven per Baltussen et al.), a real but structurally fragile and mean-reverting effect — do not extrapolate its 2023-25 magnitude; consider a WFO sensitivity that exits 30 min before close to measure how much of the edge is exactly that window. (6) Keep the existing red-team conclusion that the sample has no bear regime: drift-TIMING (long on trend days in a bull tape) is the main unfalsified confounder, and only the planned locked-forward period or a bear/flat regime can separate it from genuine trend capture.

verdict_component: Repackaged index drift does not arithmetically explain the headline number, but it plausibly explains a meaningful minority of it and one untested channel could explain far more. Over our exact window an always-long, RTH-only 1-lot NQ earned only ~$49k (25% of the +$199k 24h drift; 2023's anomalous intraday-dominant rally supplied nearly all of it), versus our $146.4k slip-0 net — and a two-sided trend machine's net-long time exposure caps unconditional drift capture at roughly $5-20k (≤15% of net); moreover our profit concentration (2024Q3+Aug, 2025 Jan ≈ 45% of net) sits in quarters where intraday drift was negative, which pure long-drift cannot produce. The surviving drift-shaped risks are (a) conditional drift-timing — long trend entries held to close in a +91% tape — which fits the long/short PF gap and the session-close bucket and cannot be separated from genuine trend capture without a bear regime or the locked-forward period, and (b) a premise flaw: "flat at 17:00 ET" is Globex session close, so the strategy may legally hold through the 16:00→9:30 window that carried 75% (~$150k/contract) of the drift — until position-hours are audited from timestamps and daily P&L is regressed on overnight/intraday NQ components, drift confounding of one-third to one-half of net cannot be excluded. Forward profitability therefore hinges on the alpha that remains after beta-carry removal, and the freeze decision should be gated on that regression, the long-only/short-only splits, and the exposure-hour audit.

findings: GRADES (audited against Bailey/López de Prado DSR [SSRN 2460551], Bailey-Borwein-LdP-Zhu PBO/CSCV [SSRN 2326253; davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf], Pseudo-Mathematics MinBTL [AMS Notices 2014], Harvey-Liu Backtesting [SSRN 2345489], and preregistration norms). Overall B−: process discipline is genuinely above published-research norm; the binding constraints are sample length and vendor degrees of freedom, which no amount of process fixes. Component grades: (1) Preregistration-before-results in git: A− — falsifiable hypotheses with mechanisms, quarantined probe runs (SW00 R09/R11), justified deviations documented in-spec; missing only an immutable external anchor (local git history is rewritable via rebase; a freeze tag proves nothing unless pushed to a remote or timestamped externally before results exist). (2) Config registry / seq-counting: B− — right structure, wrong denominator (see Gap 2), and Tier-1 native sweeps archive "summary payload" only, which permanently destroys the T×N daily-return matrix that CSCV/PBO requires (Bailey et al. 2326253). (3) WFO 12/3+18/6 purged+embargoed: C — right vocabulary, infeasible geometry (see Gap 3). (4) DSR/PBO/SPA: C+ — named in Research_Thesis.txt §12.8 but not operationalized: no trial-count definition, no SPA benchmark family specified, no data-retention plan. (5) Day-block + episode bootstraps: B+ — exactly the right dependence structure for a strategy whose losses cluster by episode; block length and stationary-bootstrap p not preregistered, and no day-of-week-stratified variant despite Thursday = 41% of net. (6) Locked-forward + freeze + no-rescue: B+ — the six no-rescue rules are best-in-class; missing a power statement (a 6–12 month locked-forward has SR-SE ≈ 1.2–1.7 and mathematically cannot confirm SR 1.4). (7) Determinism: B — 7 bit-identical runs plus penny-exact UI parity and per-trade accounting identities is sufficient for PIPELINE integrity, but determinism is orthogonal to simulation validity: it reproduces the same bias identically. TOP 5 GAPS: [GAP 1 — the baseline is not statistically significant even at N=1 trials] SR 1.39, SE 0.97 → t ≈ 1.43, one-sided p ≈ 0.076, PSR(0) ≈ 92% < 95%. Every gate in the protocol is economic (slip-1 net > 0, avg trade ≥ 2.5×RT cost) — none is statistical. Under Harvey-Liu the haircut Sharpe at any honest trial count is near zero; HLZ's t ≳ 3 bar needs ~9 years at this SR. The positive skew from top-decile concentration (32.7% of gross) helps PSR slightly but excess kurtosis hurts; compute PSR with the actual skew/kurt of daily MTM rather than assuming normality. [GAP 2 — seq-counting radically undercounts researcher DoF] The registry says "configs consumed: 1", but 90/179/5/10/true/10 arrived as the argmax of the vendor's unknown prior search, and Type-1-of-3, 1-min-of-many, session-close-exit, and NQ-of-many were all chosen after exposure to vendor materials — those are trials outside the registry. MinBTL logic (AMS Notices 2014: 5y tolerates ~45 independent trials at E[max SR]=1) implies 2.1y tolerates only a handful; the vendor's hidden search alone plausibly exceeds it. DSR computed with N=1 would be optimistic fiction. [GAP 3 — WFO geometry is infeasible on 25 months] 18/6/3-step yields exactly 1 test fold; 12/3 yields ~4 folds (~13 months OOS) — too few for CSCV (standard design: S≈8–16 blocks, ~70 splits). Also the purge/embargo is aimed at the wrong leak: trades never span sessions (flat at 17:00, verified in SW00 gate 5), so trade purging is near-vacuous; the real fold-boundary leak is the hysteresis state machine's warm-up (state persists across sessions — each test fold needs preregistered indicator burn-in or fold results will not match the continuous run). [GAP 4 — uniform cost model vs. edge concentration in the thinnest liquidity window] The entire net edge (+$189.6k on 279 session-close trades, PF 10.8) is realized by market orders at ~16:59:30 ET — after the 16:00 cash close and the 16:15–16:30 equity-futures halt, in the lowest-depth half-hour of the CME day. For 1 lot the 1-tick assumption is probably adequate, but no test in the protocol targets it, and the survivorship confound (trailing-stop trades net −$42.8k) means the SPA/Reality-Check null family must be explicitly defined to include the drift-matched random-entry-with-identical-close-machinery control (SW01b, already planned — correct) plus an intraday-long-only benchmark, not just the "frozen Type 1 benchmark" named in §12.8. [GAP 5 — freeze integrity has two silent holes] (a) The frozen baseline is defined on a back-adjusted NQU6 series; back-adjustment mutates the entire historical price path at every quarterly roll, so archived ledger hashes become irreproducible after September unless the bar-data snapshot itself is checksummed and archived (data-contract DoF — roll schedule, session template — is also absent from the registry); (b) freeze tags must be pushed/timestamped externally before results, per Gap-grade 1.
implications: KEEP: preregistration-with-mechanism discipline, quarantine convention, no-rescue rules, zero-DoF red-team experiments (SW01b/SW01c are exactly the right nulls), episode/day-block bootstrap choice, honest slip-1 basis. CHANGE NOW (cheap, urgent): (1) From the next Tier-1 sweep onward, archive full daily P&L per config, not summary payloads — otherwise PBO/CSCV is permanently impossible for everything already swept; (2) checksum and archive the raw bar series behind the frozen baseline before the September roll; (3) push signed freeze/prereg tags to a remote (or OpenTimestamps) as part of the commit ritual; (4) add a preregistered statistical gate: PSR (with empirical skew/kurt) and a bracketed Harvey-Liu haircut at N ∈ {10, 100, 1000} reported alongside every promotion, so the vendor-DoF uncertainty is displayed rather than hidden. CHANGE THE PLAN: (5) Drop 18/6 WFO (1 fold = void); replace the WFO centerpiece with CPCV on ~12 monthly blocks (test pairs → ~66 splits, many OOS paths) with indicator warm-up preregistered per fold, keeping 12/3 WFO only as a descriptive path; (6) extend the sample as the SW01c red-team item already intends — 2022 (bear regime) plus the never-examined 2025-03 → 2026-07 window, which has special status: it is the only data plausibly postdating the vendor's optimization and is therefore the only clean OOS with respect to the vendor's hidden trials — preregister it as a one-shot read before the locked-forward starts; (7) reframe the locked-forward as a disconfirmation tripwire (preregistered max-DD / losing-streak stop bounds), not a confirmation device — state in the freeze doc that at SR≈1.4 no feasible locked-forward length can statistically confirm the edge, so the promotion case must rest on mechanism evidence (SW01b drift control, session-close counterfactual SW02) plus survival of the deflation battery, not on significance. TEST NEXT: targeted cost stress applying 2–4 ticks only to session-close executions (entire edge rides on 279 fills in the 16:30–17:00 thin window); day-of-week-stratified bootstrap for the Thursday 41% concentration; define the SPA benchmark family in writing (random-entry drift control, intraday-long-only, frozen Type-1) before SW02 results are read.

verdict_component: The validation protocol is procedurally stronger than most published quant research — genuine preregistration, append-only registries, quarantining, and no-rescue rules are real and verifiable in the repo — but the audit's central finding is that no procedure can extract statistical significance that the sample does not contain: at SR 1.39 with SE 0.97 over 2.1 years, the baseline cannot reject zero skill even before deflating for the vendor's unknown prior optimization of 90/179, and the planned 18/6 walk-forward collapses to a single test fold. Forward profitability therefore cannot currently be asserted on statistical grounds at any conventional threshold; the honest posture is that this is an economically plausible, cost-surviving candidate whose entire edge sits in one structurally confounded exit channel (session-close trades in the thinnest liquidity window), pending three things the campaign can actually deliver: the drift-matched null (SW01b), the never-examined 2022 and 2025-03→2026-07 windows as the only clean OOS relative to vendor DoF, and a CPCV-plus-deflation battery run on fully archived per-config P&L. If those pass, the strategy earns a small, tripwire-guarded live allocation whose purpose is disconfirmation, not confirmation; if the drift control or the clean OOS windows fail, the DSR/MinBTL arithmetic says the prior should be that the backtest edge was selection artifact plus drift beta.

findings:
BASE RATES FROM THE LITERATURE (all sourced via WebSearch, 2026-08-06):
(1) Anomaly decay: McLean & Pontiff (Journal of Finance 2016, 97 published predictors) find returns are 26% lower out-of-sample (pure selection/overfitting bias) and 58% lower post-publication (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2156623). The 26% is the MOST CHARITABLE haircut available anywhere in the literature — it applies to academically vetted, multi-decade, cross-sectional anomalies, a far stronger evidence class than a 2.1-year vendor-indicator backtest.
(2) Practitioner haircuts: Harvey & Liu "Backtesting" (JPM 2015, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2345489) document the industry-standard 50% haircut and show the correct multiple-testing haircut is nonlinear: >50% (often much larger) for annualized SR<0.4, ≤25% for SR>1.0. Our observed daily-MTM Sharpe 1.39 nominally sits in the protected zone, BUT its SE ~0.97 means t≈1.4 (90% CI spans zero), and the vendor-tuned 90/179 parameters carry an UNKNOWN and unbudgetable trial count — exactly the case Bailey & López de Prado's False Strategy Theorem / Deflated Sharpe framework flags: expected max in-sample Sharpe grows mechanically with trials, so a marginal t≈1.4 with unknown multiplicity has DSR ≈ indistinguishable from zero (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2460551).
(3) Bank-engineered strategies (closest analog to vendor products): Suhonen, Lennkh & Perez (JPM 2017, 215 investment-bank alt-beta strategies, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2757113) find a MEDIAN 73% Sharpe deterioration backtest→live, worse by 30+ pp for more complex strategies (our dual-threshold hysteresis state machine is on the complex end).
(4) Retail-platform strategies: Wiecki et al. 2016 (888 Quantopian algos with ≥6m true OOS, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2745220) find in-sample Sharpe has R²<0.025 for predicting OOS performance — essentially uninformative — and degradation grows with amount of backtesting done.
(5) Retail futures day-trading ecology: Chague, De-Losso & Giovannetti (SSRN 3423101, Brazilian regulator data, 19,646 individuals) find 97% of those persisting >300 days in mini-index futures day trading lose money net of fees; only 1.1% out-earn minimum wage. Person-level not strategy-level, but it prices the ecosystem our vendor indicator is sold into.
(6) Forward-tracked hypothetical systems: CXO Advisory's Collective2 review found only ~18% of published systems matched/beat the S&P over the tracked window, with high infant mortality (https://www.cxoadvisory.com/investing-expertise/collective2-a-marketplace-of-trading-systems/); professional CTAs/hedge funds — with real infrastructure — still show ~7-20% annual attrition (https://www.cmegroup.com/education/files/survival-of-commodity-trading-advisors.pdf).
No credible source exists giving a direct survival rate for "NinjaTrader vendor-indicator strategies with IS PF≈1.1"; the closest proxies (items 3, 4, 6) all point the same direction: for marginal in-sample metrics, expect 50-75% Sharpe decay and near-zero predictive value of the IS point estimate itself.
APPLIED TO OUR NUMBERS: PF 1.106 at 1-tick and avg trade $40.83 (~8 NQ ticks) means the edge is mechanically dead at ~1.5 extra ticks/execution of realized slippage ($10/RT per tick); a 26% McLean-Pontiff-style haircut takes forward Sharpe to ~1.0, a Suhonen-style 73% haircut to ~0.37, and Wiecki says the point estimate barely predicts anything. Our own red-team flags (entire +$189.6k edge in 279 session-close trades PF 10.8 vs -$42.8k in trailing-stop exits; Thursday=41% of net; 3 months≈45% of net; long PF 1.20 vs short 1.07 in a doubling market; zero bear-regime coverage; vendor parameters predating our research on contaminated 2023-2025 data) collectively suggest much of the measured edge is conditional long-drift capture (hold-into-close beta), not entry alpha.
implications: CHANGE/KEEP/TEST for THIS campaign: (a) KEEP the preregistration, multiple-testing registry, WFO+DSR/PBO/SPA plan — it is exactly what the literature says separates the 73%-decay population from survivors; do NOT soften the no-rescue-tuning rule. (b) CHANGE the null hypothesis: the primary competitor model should be "conditional drift capture," not "no edge" — add a preregistered attribution test comparing the 279 session-close trades against session-close-matched RANDOM-ENTRY controls (same exit logic, day-block bootstrap); if entries add nothing vs random entries held to close, the alpha claim dies even if P&L is positive. (c) CHANGE the sample: extend the backtest to 2018-2022 (COVID crash + 2022 bear) — this data is outside the vendor's plausible tuning window and is the cheapest decisive experiment available; a strategy that is long-PF-1.20/short-PF-1.07 in a doubling market must show what it does when NQ falls 33%. (d) TEST execution reality before any capital: 2-3 months locked-forward MNQ or sim with measured per-fill slippage vs the 1-tick assumption; at $40.83/trade average, realized slippage is the single largest mechanical risk. (e) Budget position sizing off the haircut numbers, not the backtest: plan around forward Sharpe 0.3-0.7 and a max DD materially worse than -$22k (no bear regime in sample means the observed DD is a lower bound), and treat Thursday/Q3 concentration as a fragility to monitor, not a feature to exploit.

verdict_component: Honest subjective probability that the CURRENT baseline (unchanged, 1 contract, 1-tick costs) nets positive over the next 12 months: 35-55%, point estimate ~45% — and the probability that it possesses genuine transferable entry alpha (as opposed to conditional long-drift capture plus luck) is materially lower, roughly 10-20%. Reasoning: the naive frequentist read (Sharpe 1.39 → ~90% chance of a positive year) is inadmissible because (i) the t-stat is only ~1.4 with unknown vendor-tuning multiplicity, so the Deflated Sharpe is approximately zero; (ii) every relevant base-rate population (26% decay for vetted academic anomalies, median 73% decay for bank-engineered strategies, R²<0.025 predictive value in the closest retail-algo cohort) demands a haircut that pushes forward Sharpe into the 0.3-0.7 band, where a single year is close to a coin flip; and (iii) our own decomposition shows the entire net edge lives in 279 hold-into-close trades in a doubling market with zero bear-regime coverage, making the modal scenario "positive if NQ drifts up, negative if it doesn't" rather than regime-independent alpha. The three pieces of evidence that would most move this probability: (1) purged/embargoed WFO OOS results PLUS an extended 2018-2022 backtest outside the vendor tuning window — concatenated OOS PF ≥~1.05 at 1-tick with PBO<20% and survival through the 2022 bear would lift the range toward 55-70%, while OOS PF ≤1.0 or a 2022 blowup drops it to 20-35%; (2) the session-close attribution test — if Type-1 entries beat session-close-matched random-entry controls (day-block bootstrap p<0.05) the alpha probability roughly doubles, and if they don't, the strategy is repriced as leveraged conditional beta; (3) measured live/sim execution — 2-3 months of MNQ forward fills showing realized slippage ≤1 tick/execution preserves the case, while >1.5 ticks mechanically eliminates the $40.83 average trade regardless of signal quality.
